links.outcome: Readability of chatbot responses to fibromyalgia questions (Flesch Reading Ease)
links.effect: Readability scores indicated university-level complexity; ChatGPT-4o had the lowest Reading Ease score (11.3 ± 11.2) and Copilot the highest (30.3 ± 13.2).
links.quote: Readability scores indicated university-level complexity, with ChatGPT-4o having the lowest Reading Ease score (11.3 ± 11.2) and Copilot the highest (30.3 ± 13.2).

links.outcome: Citation consistency in chatbot fibromyalgia responses
links.effect: Citation inconsistencies were noted across chatbots, alongside low quality information (EQIP 20.6 to 40.5) and moderate misinformation levels; no citation-verification practice was tested.
links.quote: Gemini, Copilot, and Perplexity AI showed better quality, but citation inconsistencies, readability challenges, and misinformation risks highlight the need for refinement beyond the hype.

screen.reason: Evaluates the quality, readability, and accuracy of AI chatbots answering patient queries about fibromyalgia, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
